key_insight: PG-KINN improves physics-informed PDE solving by pairing a KAN trial space with a Petrov-Galerkin weak form, reducing derivative burden and improving accuracy/conditioning over strong-form and energy-form approaches.
engineering_relevance: This makes the method especially useful for solid mechanics problems with nonlinear constitutive behavior, singularities, complex geometries, and inverse parameter identification.
method: KAN as the trial network with learnable spline activations
Independent compactly supported piecewise-polynomial test functions
Gauss-Legendre quadrature with integration by parts for element-wise weak residuals
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent gains over MLP baselines and state-of-the-art KAN-based strong/energy/inverse methods across benchmarks including crack singularities, stress concentration, hyperelasticity, inverse media identification, and complex geometries.
watch_item: Performance depends on a correct Petrov-Galerkin setup and quadrature/test-space design, which may add implementation complexity and sensitivity to basis choices.
paper_title: PG-KINN: A Physics-Informed Petrov-Galerkin Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for Solving Forward and Inverse PDEs
